answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fraud. Splitting one attacker’s resources across a hundred identities does not create a hundred free votes: every identity needs capital at risk, and coordinated false claims expose all their bonds to loss. The violet team can audit a glacier shipment against basalt sensor records, making fabricated identities costly without relying on names or one central registry.
